name: Rosy Pink
lede: Rosy Pink is a vivid deep pink from the ISCC-NBS dictionary; the one useful book note is about a different rosy pink, the pale lake made from brazilwood.

sections.title: A dictionary pink
sections.body: Rosy Pink is an ISCC-NBS 1955 dictionary name, and the swatch falls in the deep-pink block [2]. It is also listed in the xkcd survey of 2010 [2]. It is a lively cousin of [[pink]], [[rose]], [[salmon]] and [[coral]], more saturated than the pale pinks the phrase often suggests [2].

sections.title: The rosy pink of a lake pigment
sections.body: In Ball's history of pigments, brazilwood red was made by boiling the wood in lye or alum, then precipitating a lake [1]. Adding chalk, white lead, marble dust or powdered eggshell gave a rosy pink pigment, which in England was called roset [1]. Ball adds that some historians think brazil was the foremost red lake of the Middle Ages, but he cautions that no medieval painting has been positively shown to contain it [1]. This is the sense of rosy pink that painters knew, a paler and chalkier color than our swatch [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: No painting in our archive has this color covering at least 1% of its canvas, as photographed [3]. That describes this archive, not painting as a whole [3].
